utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Judge Parker is unable to sit today, so pursuant to the Rules Judge Thelin and I will sit alone. Good afternoon, sir. Will you please read the affirmation on the card that is in front of you. Can you read what is on the card in front of you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. And I think Mr. Saxon is going to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, this witness will be led by my colleague, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So it will be Mr. Dobbyn. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honours for the record the witness is calling Witness M-085, Miodrag Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, are you an ethnic Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in 2001 were you an active police officer in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you still a member of the Macedonian police today?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court how long you have been a Macedonian police officer for?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: 29 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what position do you hold now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I am a police administrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to 2001 and ask you some questions about that time-period. Now as a police officer during 2001 were you assigned to the police station for external physical security of buildings which was formerly known as PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in 2001 what was your position at that station?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I was police administrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall in 2001 what your duties were as a administrator at that station?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Preparation of lists, maintaining records, and keeping maintenance of the warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what sort of things were contained in the warehouses that you maintained?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Weapons and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And in 2001 were you the only person at PSOLO who dealt with the issuance of weapons and other equipment to police officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall if in 2001 you actually did issue weapons and equipment to reservist police officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall if during 2001, and continuing into 2003, there was a increased numbering of reservists were activated and issued with weapons when compared with prior years?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall if the equipment that was issued to reservists from PSOLO was different from that that was issued to active police officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, the equipment was the same, the clothing, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we can take this perhaps a step at a time. What was the type of equipment that was issued to police reservists?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Where any weapons issued to police reservists?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you recall if, in 2001, there was a record-keeping procedure of some sort with respect to the weapons and equipment issued to reservist police officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And how exactly did you keep record of what was issued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: We maintained a list on forms that have been prescribed for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to ask you now about June 2001. Do you recall at that time there being a special unit of the Ministry of Interior called the Lions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would it refresh your recollection if I showed you a statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 7th of August, 2004?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're trying to ask me. Can you clarify this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. I asked you whether you could recall there being a special unit named the Lions and your response was no. I'm asking, in light of that, whether it would refresh your recollection to look at a earlier statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: About the Lions, I started working since November when they were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And just to clarify your answer, you started working since November of what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at what time, to your knowledge, were the Lions formed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: November or December, and there was a law for the establishment and this is when Goran Stojkov called me in order for me to maintain the -- the payment -- the payroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So do you recall any groups of volunteers who you believe to be from the Lions unit coming to PSOLO for weapons after 20th of June, 2001 and through July 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Volunteers came, but they were not from the Lions. Those were volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Was it your belief at that time that they were from the Lions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: At that time, nobody even mentioned the word "Lions."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just at this point, sorry I didn't do this earlier, but I do have binders for this witness of exhibits that we should distribute at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, I'd like to draw your attention now to July of 2001 and specifically to the date of 25th of July, 2001. Do you recall if you were on duty that day at the police station PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If it was a working day, then I was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would it refresh your recollection, would you be able to make yourself certain in you were shown the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is no problem. I can see the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have hard copies of Mr. Stojanovski's statement to distribute. It has also been uploaded into e-court, I believe. But if those copies could be shown to Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: -- do you recall giving this statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 7th of August, 2004?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I spoke to Mr. Thomas. We only had a conversation, because at the very beginning I can see here that I am here voluntarily to give a statement. However, I was ordered by the MOI to go there. It was not voluntarily. And Mr. Thomas told me that we will only have a conversation and this is going to be left at it, and I did not agree for this to be distributed to anybody else. When he asked me to sign the statement, I asked for the statement to be prepared in Macedonian language. However, he insisted that I should signed statement in English so that, first of all, the interpreter was reading it and we had a long conversation, because he told me that he spoke the Serbo-Croat language. Well, we had a mutual conversation and female interpreter was interpreting. At the end when she started reading the statement, there were many mistakes and he started correcting these mistakes on the computer. After we finished, it was around in the evening, around 8.00 or 9.00. I was kept there for the whole day and he asked me to sign the statement. I asked for a statement in Macedonian language to read it and to see what it was written down. For the second time, the statement was not read to me, and I told him, since they insist, and I was there present during the conversation upon the MOI order, and I told him that I will sign the statement but I do not recognise this statement because it was not made in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if I can ask you, Mr. Stojanovski --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If I can ask you, Mr. Stojanovski, do you see your signature at the bottom of the first page and at the bottom of each page therefore?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you can look at page 7. Do you see a heading in English which says, "Witness acknowledgment"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And perhaps if I follow this in the Macedonian version which is on page 9, do you see where it says: "This statement has been read over to me in the Macedonian language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see your signature underneath that dated 7th of August, 2004?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I wonder if we could show through e-court copies of the statements in Macedonian and English. And in particular, I would like to go to paragraph 16, which is on page 4 of the English version and also page 4 of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you can just look at the first line of paragraph 16, Mr. Stojanovski. Do you see where it says: "On 25 July 2001 the Kometa people came with Johan Tarculovski to PSOLO." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So does this refresh your recollection as to whether you were working on the 25th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall if some persons came to PSOLO for weapons and equipment on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, some people came over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall who those people were?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Those people were, as they told us, they were in police of Kometa.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did you recognise any particular individuals with that group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Only Goce Ralevski. I think I recognised Goce Ralevski. But I didn't know whether he works in Kometa. I knew him from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And where do you know him from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: His brother used to work with me as a commander for the security of the parliament. So through his brother I was -- I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall if Johan Tarculovski was present at PSOLO on the 25th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Johan Tarculovski, I saw him only in the yard of the police station underneath the tree, how he was standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall how this group of people, how you learned that this group of people were from Kometa?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: From themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall exactly what sort of organisation or group Kometa was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you clarify what you really mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: For example, do you know if Kometa was a social group, was it a business of some sort? Do you know what business, if any, they had?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: It was a security agency.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall who the head of Kometa was in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: According to what they were saying, a person called Zoran was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall if this person named Zoran was present at PSOLO on either 25th of July or 26th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: He was present there with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you know or do you recall Zoran's last name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this time are you able to recall how many Kometa people came to the station to receive weapons and equipment on 25 July 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I am not aware of the correct number. They were outside in the yard, and this is where they were waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could just take a step back for a moment. The head of Kometa we had been talking about, the person named Zoran, do you recall whether he had a nickname at all?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall distributing weapons and equipment to the members of Kometa who came to PSOLO on 25 July 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this time I would like to show the witness a document. It has been marked for identification as P00436. And it is also in tab 2 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you see the document that is on the screen before you and is also at tab 2 of the binder in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you tell -- tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a list of issued weapons and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall if you were the person who developed this form, the form used for this list?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall using the same type of forms to document distribution of weapons to members of the Lions unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: First, we issued equipment to the volunteers, and later on the Lions. For the Lions, the weapons was distributed in Idrizovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now if you could look at the list you will see there are numbers next to the name of each person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could go to the last page of the document in each language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You'll see, Mr. Stojanovski, that it is numbered up to 84. Do you recall if all --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall if all 84 of the people listed on this list received weapons at PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, not all of them were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would I be correct in interpreting this to say that those with numbers and entries next to their names are the ones who did receive weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, do you recall, Mr. Stojanovski, who ordered the distribution of these weapons and equipment to the Kometa members?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: My superior, Georgi Mitrev.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall if back in 2001, after receiving a order to distribute weapons and equipment to a person, whether you would ask that person for ID?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what would you do after receiving a form of identification from each person?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I issued them weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would you make a note of their identification anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This was done by my colleague, Sarenkovski Vojko, who assisted me when we were handing out the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall if -- sorry. Do you recall how on the 25th of July, 2001 you determined which particular individuals were to be issued with weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not decide for this. This would be something that would be ordered by my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So the list that you have in front of you and the list that is on the screen, who decided which names should go on to this list?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: How do you mean, which names would appear on the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, as you see, there's a list here with 84 names on it. How did those names come to be on this list? Where did these names come from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: They came around lunch-time and they were waiting in the yard of the station. Around 3.00, 4.00 p.m., one of the employees in Kometa had a list of the employees, and he offered this list to me, so if this list is approved, then this would be the list included in my own list and that is why we had this large number of people. This doesn't mean that all of them were present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And if we look at the list there are some names with blank spaces next to them. Do you recall why these people were not issued with weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Because they did not appear at all to be issued with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the first page of the document, please. Looking at the Macedonian version, Mr. Stojanovski, do you see your signature on that front page?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is that your handwriting which says, "I hereby confirm that I personally compiled this list pursuant to a list that the Kometa employees gave me before --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Just to finish it, I'll complete. It says: "Before I started issuing them with weapons." And your answer to that was yes, I understand. Mr. Stojanovski, do you recall how long it took to you distribute these weapons and equipment to the Kometa members?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In the evening, around 9.00 or 9.30, so 2130 or 2200 hours and then after that we broke up because it was late and then we told the others that they should come the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did the others return the next day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the following day I continued issuing weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall ever handing out weapons to any other security companies at any time before this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Not companies. Not in a group fashion to companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So this was the first time you had handed out weapons to a security company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: They came as volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: My question was: Is this the first time that you had handed out weapons to members of a security company as a group.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall if you issued temporary identification cards to the Kometa members that you provided equipment to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not issue cards and issuing of cards was not my competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you know if they were issued by anyone else at PSOLO on that date?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you recall if you issued temporary or anyone at PSOLO issued temporary identification cards to any reserve personnel that you armed at around this time, July 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And just to clarify, does that mean no, no identification cards were issued; or no, you cannot recall?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not issue and I don't know if anyone else issued them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Can you recall if there came a time when reserve personnel who received equipment did start to be issued with temporary identification cards?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. An order for that, we received from the defence preparations, but I can't tell you when.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if we could perhaps return to the witness statement of Mr. Stojanovski. I'd like to go to paragraph 29, which is on page 6 of the English version and also page 6 of the Macedonian. And if we could just perhaps focus in on paragraph 29 of each. And it says there: "Generally, I did not issue any receipts to the volunteers for the weapons they were handed out. Being asked for temporary ID cards issued to reserve personnel, I say that at the time the Kometa people were armed, we didn't issue any temporary ID cards. Only in fall of 2001 we started to issue temporary police ID cards but only to regular police reservists." So, Mr. Stojanovski, does this refresh your recollection as to when temporary ID cards came to be issued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And was that in the fall of 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: It might have been in the fall. We had received a memo about this from the defence. You can check this and verify. And I was misunderstood here. It should not be "we started," but "It has started." It was not us who started issuing because I'm not in charge of this and I never issued those. This is written here incorrectly. Maybe I was misunderstood by Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. But do I take it that it was your understanding that the issuing of identification cards started later in 2001 than on the 25th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no, it was later and it was ordered by, I think it was some of the foreign representatives who urged for this and then the defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter thinks it is Defence Preparation.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: -- unit started issuing cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'd like now to ask a couple of questions specifically about the 25th and 26th of July, 2001. Do you recall what type of weapons you distributed to the Kometa employees at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, as to any other volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could we please pull up P00436 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if you look at the second column you will see that it is headed: Automatic rifle. What do the letters and numbers entered into that column indicate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Which column do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you see the second column in the table? Again, this is if you're looking on the hard copy it's under number 2, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Where it is written automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: That was the number of the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Was any ammunition issued to the members of Kometa who came on 25 and 26 July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, 120 bullets each.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall if you distributed any other equipment to the Kometa employees?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall if all of these uniforms that you issued to the Kometa employees were exactly the same?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: They had the same tailoring, while the shade might have differed, depending on the fabric used, but they looked the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you recall if the uniforms had any police insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. On the sleeves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you describe the insignia that was on the sleeves of the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: On the one side, it is written "Police," and on the other it is the patch. Again, on the other there is the narrow patch and on the other side there is the wide patch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And were these patches on all of the uniforms that you issued on 25 and 26 July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on all uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojanovski, are you familiar with the piece of equipment known as a Zolja?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Have you -- do you recall if you've ever heard what a Zolja is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I have never issued. Well, the name, yes, I have heard the name. Just the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And so is my understanding correct that you never issued Zoljas to any of the members from Kometa?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I could not have issued because there were no such weapons in my warehouse, and I don't know what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall if there were any other locations within the Ministry of Interior from where people may have been able to obtain Zoljas?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't know. From the warehouse of the Ministry of the Interior, if the officer in charge there issued them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall if the Lions unit had stores of Zoljas?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: At the time when Kometa was issued with weapons, since the unit Lions did not exist, I was the only one issuing volunteers with weapons, so the unit Lions, there was no other warehouse, they could not have issued weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'd like to look at some of the names on the list of people who received weapons now. If we could please look at number 21 on the list. On the English this is page 4; in the Macedonian, it's on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, next to number 21 do you see the name Zoran Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You testified earlier that you knew the leader of Kometa to be a person named Zoran. Do you have any idea if this is the same person?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. From the conversation with him, I heard that the person is charged with Zoran, but I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction in line 17/14 instead "If the officer had issued them," "If the officer had them in stock." It refers to the Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: From looking at the list can you tell what equipment, if any, you issued to this person called Zoran Jovanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I have issued only automatic rifles and camouflage uniforms, nothing more to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And was any ammunition issued also?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, ammunition. Automatic rifles, ammunition and camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could look now at the next name on the list, at number 22. Do you see the name Vlado Janev?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you know anyone who goes by the nickname Kunta?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And from looking at the list, can we see that Vlado Janev was also issued with a weapon, ammunition, camouflage uniform and boots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could look at the next name now, number 23, Aleksandar Janevski. Do you see that name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recognise that name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you know who goes by the nickname Vlatko?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can he see that Aleksandar Janevski was also issued with weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could now move to number 30 which is on page 5 of the English version and page 2 of the Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At number 30, do you see the name Trajce Kuzmanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: But this person was also issued with weapons and equipment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could move on to page 9 in the English version; page 3 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you see the name next to the number 54, Goce Ralevski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall testifying earlier that this was someone that you knew?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And was it your -- you also testified that it was your understanding that all the people on the list were members of Kometa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is what I was told by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And we can see also that he was issued with a weapon and ammunition; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If you look at the -- the entries on the same page for number 51, Beni Popevski; number 55, Marjan Stevkovski; and number 56, Ljupco Sivakov. Do you see those names?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And can you see that it appears that their equipment was all returned by a person by the name of Goce or Goce R. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could go back to page 4 of the English and page 1 of the Macedonian, please. And if you look at the entries for the people we discussed earlier, Zoran Jovanovski, Vlado Janev and Aleksandar Janevski, do you see also that their weapons and equipment was all returned by someone by the name of Goce, or Goce R?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you have -- sorry. Do you know why this person appeared to be responsible for returning so many weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: When they started returning the equipment, since I knew Goce and I phoned him, that he needed to return the equipment, he said, "If people come there personally, good, and if not, I will return the equipment to you. I will take it from everyone and return it to you." So Goce brought the weapons to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So Goce was a person who would be able to retrieve all of the weapons from the Kometa members; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: He could have sent them to come, and probably he was able to take it from them, because he did bring everything to me, so that I had the equipment I issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek to tender the document marked for identification as P00436.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under the same number but as Exhibit P436, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you recall if you were ever interviewed in relation to the investigation into the events in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Whom are you referring at precisely? I was interviewed by Mr. Thomas only.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall if you were ever interviewed by any of the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: When I took this list, when I was invited to the MOI, there was some committee there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this time could we please show a report. It's a part of the what has been marked for identification as P00379. And what I'm specifically looking for is pages 10 to 18 of the Macedonian in e-court, and the ERN for the English version is N000-8909 to N000-8917-ET, and it's also contained in tab 6 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you see the document in front of you, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that on the top left-hand corner it says: "Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Macedonia, investigation committee about the events and happenings in the village, Ljuboten. And it is dated 25 November 2003?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And under that you see the heading: "Information on the activities undertaken by the investigation committee about the events and happenings in the village, Ljuboten."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, if we could move to page 2 of the English version. And this is -- sorry. This is on page 2 of the Macedonian version also. If we could move to the bottom of the Macedonian page. Mr. Stojanovski, do you see the paragraph which starts: "The same day a conversation was carried out." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this states: "The same day a conversation was carried out with the owner of the security agency Kometa, Zoran Jovanovski, alias Bucuk. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we could now move down a couple of lines, and I think we would need to move to the next page of the Macedonian version. And if we could move to the top of that page. Do you see where it starts: "Otherwise, the weapon ..." Can you see that on the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this states: "Otherwise the weapon, an automatic rifle and two magazines he entrusted at PSOLO for which there is written documentation." Do you follow that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether the person referred to here as Zoran Jovanovski, the owner of Kometa, is the same person you have mentioned in your testimony as Zoran, the head of Kometa?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I don't know what this here is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, do you recall being shown the list of persons you had issued weapons to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, that is fine. There is the name Zoran Jovanovski. That is the fact. I'm not disputing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Could we move to the -- to page 3 of the English version, and it's page 4 of the Macedonian. And it's the second paragraph in the English version, and the first full paragraph in the Macedonian. And do you see where the first full paragraph in the Macedonian starts: "In the conversation with Ljube Krstevski ... " Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And could you then move on to the second line in that paragraph where it starts: "On 11 August 2001." Do you see where I am?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that states: "On 11 August 2001 without his knowledge, around 80 people arrived dressed in police uniforms who he did not know and he was informed by inspect Ljupce Gjurcevski that these persons are employed at Kometa and among them was the owner Zoran Jovanovski, alias Bucuk. Then Krstevski explained that this group of persons was mainly armed, that is, they had weapons entrusted to them before at the PSOLO, while without weapons there were 10 to 11 persons." Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is this consistent with your recollection and your testimony that you provided weapons to members of Kometa at PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And we could now move to the last paragraph on page 6 of the English version, and this is the second paragraph on page 8 of the Macedonian. And this paragraph starts: "After this, a conversation was carried out ..." Do you see where I am on that page?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that states: "After this, a conversation was carried out with Trajce Kuzmanovski too employed as a security guard at the Swiss embassy through the security agency Kometa." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if we can move on down approximately three sentences to where it starts: "To the question ..." Do you see where I am now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that states: "To the question whether he was entrusted with weapons, police uniform and whether he has ever been to the police station Cair" --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at this point can we move on to the next page in English,.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: -- "Kuzmanovski replied that during July 2001 he asked on his own to be entrusted with an automatic rifle, four magazines, and a uniform at the PSOLO, which he later returned unused because he was not engaged by the police to take part in any activities." Did you see that, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And again on the list of persons you issued weapons to, do you recall seeing the name Trajce Kuzmanovski? Do you recall having seen that name?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If it is there, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if you can look at the hard copy in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's already, Kuzmanovski. It's there, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this person was also issued with weapons and other equipment, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I'd now like to move on to the third paragraph on page 7 of the English. And this is the first full paragraph on page 9 of the Macedonian. And this starts: "Radojko Lozanovski ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, Radojko Lozanovski yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it states: "Radojko Lozanovski, administrator at the department for Internal affairs Cair, and Miodrag Stojanovski, administrator at the PSNFOO, during the events in Ljuboten this police station had been called PSOLO, have been also invited for a conversation in order to provide records of the persons who in this period have been entrusted with police uniforms and weapons." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And were you invite to the appear before this investigation committee?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And did you in fact appear before the committee?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And was the information that you provided this committee truthful and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, about what they were asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could move on to the following paragraph which starts: "Stojanovski, on the other hand ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for interrupting my learned colleague, but I believe that it would be fair regarding the previous question that was asked, maybe we should ask him what he stated in front of the committee and then read the text afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm planning on reading Mr. Stojanovski's statement to him and he can comment on it after that point, if he does not feel it's accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you see where it states: "Stojanovski, on the other hand, explained that on 25 and 26 July, 2001, a large group from the agency Kometa led by Johan Tarculovski asked the commander of PSOLO, Mitrev Georgi, to be entrusted with weapons, after consultations the commander made with executives from the security sector, he ordered Stojanovski to entrust these persons with weapons. They had submitted list from which half of the persons were entrusted with weapons on 25 July, and the other half on 26 July 2001, after which all of them were sent to CO KOB to join the other volunteers and to fill in questionnaires for reserve police statements. All of them during the year of 2002 have completely returned the weapons." Did you see that, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is this a accurate summary of the information you provided to the investigative committee?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: In general, with the exception of this led by Johan Tarculovski because I could only see Johan standing in the yard beneath the tree at the station, and I haven't seen when -- them when arrived, Johan was standing in the yard and he used to come up over there quite often because, as a station, we provide security for residencies where the president, the prime minister and other guests lived and they are quite near to the station so he had regular cooperation with the commander of this particular unit that provides for security of residencies where the late president, Mr. Trajkovski, used to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Stojanovski, just to clarify, are you saying that did you not tell the committee that Johan Tarculovski was leading this group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I can't tell you because Johan was standing in the yard of the station. I didn't see them when they arrived. I could see only people in the yard. Johan did not enter. He didn't contact me and he did not enter the room where the superiors were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll move on at this point. As a result of speaking to the investigative committee, do you recall if you prepared any type of report or note?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I wrote a statement, a written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: If we could please show what is part of MFI P00379, and the part I'm looking for is on page 25 of the Macedonian. The English ERN is N000-8924-ET and it is also in tab 5 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask we believe that the Defence counsel has his microphone on still. Please can it be turned off? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you see the document on the screen in front of you, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, I have a statement handwritten and I signed it. I signed it before the committee in -- at the MOI. This is a Official Note. I have a written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, looking at this Official Note, do you see at the top where it says: "MVR of the Republic of Macedonia, sector for NFOO, PSNFOO submitted by staff sergeant Miodrag Stojanovski, policeman administrator, 20 November 2003, Skopje." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now that appears to indicate that you prepared this Official Note, Mr. Stojanovski. Did you prepare this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is no signature of mine here, as far as I can see it. I only recollect that I wrote a statement. I did not prepare a Official Note. I was asked at the very same place by the committee to prepare a written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, if we can move to what it says on the Official Note. You'll see it says: "On 25 July 2001, a group from the Kometa agency, led by Johan Tarculovski, employed at the security sector of the RM MVR arrived at the PS OOV. They presented a list to commander Georgi Mitrev and asked to be issued with weapons as volunteer police reservists. The commander, having consulted his superiors at the security sector, ordered me to issue the weapons. Half of the men from the list were issued with weapons on 25 July 2001 and the other half on 26 July 2001, after which they were sent to the CO KOB to join other volunteers and fill out the questionnaires for police reservists. The list of volunteers issued with weapons is enclosed in the attachment. All items were issued were returned by the persons from the list in 2002." Do you see that, Mr. Stojanovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is this the same information that it states in the note from the investigative committee that you provided?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of "led by" and they contacted the commander Mitrev Georgi with the list. They did not come to the commander with the list. Who actually entered there, I'm not aware. However, they did not have a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Having gone through --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Everything else is just fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So having gone through this list, does this refresh your recollection as to whether you were the person who prepared this Official Note now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The Official Note was not prepared by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Does this look like the standard form of a Official Note that would be prepared at your police department?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you've testified --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And am I correct in understanding your testimony that the majority of this note, with the exception of one point, is a accurate description of the information you provided to the committee?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I remember, the complete material of the second committee was proposed to be accepted and the Defence counsel presented numerous arguments as a result of the comment from the counsel the -- the Prosecution gave a written statement and we reacted and that is why we decided and we believe that this is a material that a decision has to be made by the counsel [as interpreted]. And regarding this last document, although the part of the content was recognised by the witness, he did not recognise the document as a document that he has prepared. The document was not signed by the witness -- I apologise. In line 18, it says that decision should be made by the Defence counsel, and I believe that I said and this is what correct, we expect the decision by the Chamber. So for individual documents we agree that they can be agreed but in any indication, the complete material is this -- that the Chamber will make a decision afterwards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would object for this written documents to be accepted in evidence, because the witness was -- did not confirm it. He said that he did not prepare this Official Note in the major part of the text, the most important informations were not confirmed by him, and that is why I believe that this written document should not be tendered into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber, indeed, recollects that this is part of a larger motion that is still before it and it reserves its decision on this point, to be delivered together with the decision on the entirety of the motion. So it is still marked for identification, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Perhaps if we could go back to the prior document, which, again, is part of MFI 379, pages 10 to 18 in the Macedonian. And it is N000-8909 to 8917 the English. And if we could to go to the last paragraph on the first page in the English and it is the first full paragraph on page 2 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you see the paragraph starts: "With regard to the question."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't have it in front of me. I still have the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: My apologies. Okay. Do you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Oh, Your Honours I realise also that this is also the subject of our motion to have it admitted and because it refers to a statement of one of the accused, my intention at this time is not to read this into the record but rather to have the witness read it over to himself, and I will ask him to make a comment as this may come to the weight of the document later on, if it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood it well, my learned colleague, he would like for the witness to declare regarding a part of a document in -- if I am mistaken, I would like for this to be confirmed with respect to my learned colleague, are you going to ask additional questions regarding the document that was shown on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry. As I was stating, I will be asking the witness to view certain passages on this document but not read them into the record and I will ask for his comment on those passages which are in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Your Honour, I will object to this type of questioning of the witness. My learned colleague has asked several questions related to this information. According to my opinion, the correct manner of questioning would be, first of all, to determine whether the witness has ever seen this information; and whether he is aware of this information, that it was prepared; then whether he knows if the persons mentioned in this information have been interviewed; and only then maybe to read it and to find out whether this coincides with his observations. We did not object when the Prosecutor has shown the part relating to the witness himself because he could recollect and he could tell the Trial Chamber his own opinion. Regarding the other passages of the information, I don't think that this is the correct of interviewing the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully concur with the objection provided by my colleague Residovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will uphold the objection. It is indeed part of a decision that still has to be rendered by the Trial Chamber about the admissibility of this particular piece of evidence, so the Trial Chamber does not think it to be proper to ask further questions on this point. Will you please proceed Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I will move on. If we could now show 65 ter 653, which is in tab 7 of today's binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you see the document that's on the screen in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at the top it is headed telegram, Ministry of Interior for the Republic of Macedonia, Cabinet of the Minister?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: It is dated 28 July 2001, Skopje. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And then you'll see that it's addressed to various departments within the Ministry of Interior. And if you look through that, you will see that it is also addressed to your department in 2001, PSOLO. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And this thing goes on to state: "We would like to inform that you all head of organisational units as of today (28 July 2001) for the reason that the security situation has deteriorate in the country, the use of annual leaves of the employees at the Ministry of Internal Affairs are cut short, which has been approved by telegram number 3792/1933 from 17 July 2001. All employees that are on annual leave shall be informed immediately to return to their work." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you see that there's a signature at the bottom and above that, it is written Ljube Boskoski, Minister of Internal Affairs; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall being informed during the crisis period at some time around late July 2001 that employees of the Ministry of Interior would not be allowed to take any annual leave at that time? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a obligation of the superior, to inform all the employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And were you informed of that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not use the annual leave. I was working so there was no need for me to be informed. There is a unit on duty. They received the telegram, they record it, then the telegram is given to the superior and he, through the duty unit and through the commanders of the separate units would inform all the employees. Since I was on duty, I was working. There was no need for me to be informed about this particular telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time that other employees were not able to take annual leave?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I am quite sure I was aware, probably I have heard that from the people on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P489, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And at this time I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dobbyn. I think it's time for a break now. We will adjourn --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic. I'm the Defence counsel for Mr. Boskoski. Before I start asking you some questions related to your testimony, I would like to ask you one thing; namely, I understand the language that you are speaking, and you probably also understand the questions that I will ask you in the Bosnian language. However, my questions and your answers need to be interpreted by the interpreters, so that Their Honours and the colleagues in the courtroom are able to follow my questions and your answers to them. Therefore, I ask you to wait for my question to be interpreted and own then answer it. This would be the best way for you to assist the Trial Chamber and the interpreters. Have you understood this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, is it correct that you have graduated from the secondary school in 1970?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have served your conscription military service in the JNA between 1975 and 1977 in Pristina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague the Prosecutor you stated that you work for the police for 29 years. My question is whether it is correct that immediately after having served your conscription military service in 1977, you started working in the police of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your first post was actually in the unit known as PSOLO, the Police Station for Security of Facilities and Persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojanovski, in order for to us be precise, is it correct that in 2001 the real title your police station was Police Station for Security of Governmental Facilities and the Diplomatic Consular Representative Offices but, still it was colloquially known as PSOLO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by my colleague you also stated that in 2001 you were working as an administrator within PSOLO. However, I'm asking you whether it is correct that for the first five years of your work, of your career in PSOLO you were actually a ordinary police officer and after that, until the present day you work as a administrator. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although you did say something about the work of your police station, I will ask you to answer a few more questions. Is it correct that the main task of your police station was to provide security for the governmental institutions but also to provide security for the foreign embassies, consulates, and residences?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In -- if I were to say that the intergovernmental organisations, the facilities, the buildings that belonged to the state of the Republic of Macedonia such as the parliament, the government building, the buildings of the ministries, banks, then this would be the accurate descriptions of the buildings that you had the duty to provide security for; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Stojanovski, that your sector, your police station, was within the sector for security, while the sector for security was a part of the bureau of public security. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: PSOLO, so your police station, was rather large, and in 2001 it consisted of nine sections, for instance section for protection of governmental buildings, then unit for protection of the parliament, unit for security of embassies, et cetera; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that your superior officer was Georgi Mitrev. Is it correct that in 2001 he was the commander of your police station, of PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: His immediate superior was Vasilevski Borce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And above Vasilevski Borce, so the superior of the entire sector for security in 2001, was Zivko Gacevski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering your answer that your sector for security was within the bureau for public security, is it correct that also the unit for defence preparations, the one that you mentioned answering questions of my learned friend, was also within the public security bureau?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were working as an administrator. Apart from the commander of the police station, Georgi Mitrev, you had, as your superiors also Krstevski Dusko deputy commander of the police station, and Georgsevski, Gorgi, assistant to the commander of the police station. Am I right when saying this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In line 14, I said that he was "assistant", it was interpreted as "civilian", but it is now corrected as "assistant".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if I say that your post of administrator you carried out your duties pursuant to the law but also pursuant to the rule books that the minister or the government would pass in relation to the performance of the tasks within the Ministry of Interior, as well as pursuant to the annual operational plan that you had adopted within the police station, then that would be the basis for you to carry out your duties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from these general acts on the basis of which you carried out your duties you carried out your duties also on the basis of instructions or ordered by your immediate superiors; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your rather long experience within the Ministry of Interior, career of 29 years, you, or any other officer who was directly carrying out duties and tasks, never received a order from the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this "no" mean that you never received any order from the minister?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No. I have never received any order apart from my -- from my superior officer, Mitrev Georgi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the same time is it correct, Mr. Stojanovski, that you were directly responsible to your superior, to your immediate superior, the police station commander for the proper and legal carrying out of duties?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, actually, if you or any other officer would fail to perform their duties pursuant to the law and the rules, it was only the direct superior officer, the one who could collect data about that failure to perform tasks, and it was only the immediate superior, the one could instigate a disciplinary procedure. Is my understanding of the procedure correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if that happened, then a normal disciplinary procedure would be run, as prescribed by the rules of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the questions of my learned friend, you stated that your tasks were to compile and to archive lists and to be in charge of the warehouses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, if I understood you well, you maintained the records, certain records in the police station, and you took care about the warehouses that the police station had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Within your police station, there was -- there were many warehouses. Is that correct? Warehouse for weapons, for ammunition, for uniforms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: One warehouse for weapons and one warehouse for clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you answered the question of my colleague, the Prosecutor, you stated: "I issued only automatic rifles." My question is: Is it correct that you in the warehouses of PSOLO had only certain types of weapon, namely, automatic rifles of Yugoslav or Ukrainian make; and pistols made by Zastava, model M-57; a calibre 7.62 millimetres; and for the regular police, also pistols Zastava of 9 millimetres calibre. Are those the weapons you had in your warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, you never had in the warehouse any rifles of Chinese make; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There were never such guns there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never had Thompson rifles also?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No, no, never. We never had such rifles at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also if I understood you well, you never had Zoljas at the police station, and therefore you were not able to issue Zoljas to anyone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the lists shown to you by my learned friend, it could be seen clearly that the persons who were issued weapons by you at the 25th and 26th were also issued with uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I may reframe your statement, you stated that they were ordinary camouflage uniforms that could have had difference in the shades of colour and they also had the standard police patches on them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you something now, Mr. Stojanovski. Is it correct that the Macedonian language has only one alphabet, the Cyrillic alphabet is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the letter that would be written in Latin alphabet as the letter "P" would be read in the Cyrillic alphabet as the letter "R"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the marking on a certain object, a uniform or anything else that would -- had the capital "R" or a "PM" in Latin alphabet, that would mean Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask you now to show the witness the exhibit, first the exhibit P15. I would like to ask you to zoom in to these patch on the sleeve.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what is written here on this patch?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: "Police."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the first patch is actually the letter "P", in Cyrillic alphabet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show the witness the Exhibit P35. Could we please zoom in on to the patch.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see here, Mr. Stojanovski, there is -- there are the letters "R" and "M" here in the middle of this laurel. So is my understanding correct if I say that this is abbreviation for the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Logically, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if anyone sees a patch of this type on a uniform, then they could only read the Republic of Macedonia, they could only read this as meaning Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise if it should be written the police of the Republic of Macedonia, in a given patch, then, first, those should be -- this marking that is in the second row from above, that is the letter "P" in the Cyrillic alphabet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So finally the marking "RM", if somebody saw that on a uniform, can mean only the Republic of Macedonia and could not indicate whether the uniform is a police uniform, an army uniform, or uniform of any other body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Within your duties, as you already stated and repeated, was also the issuance of weapons that your police station had in stock in the warehouse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, as well as the other police stations, issued those weapons pursuant to the instruction on issuance of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the questions by my learned colleague, you stated that you had received a order from the police station commander and I'm asking whether it is correct that pursuant to the instruction on issuance of weapons the police station commander was the person responsible to issue weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that from your warehouse the weapons were distributed not only to the regular but also to the reserve police forces and in 2001 also to the volunteers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regards to this, Mr. Stojanovski, I would like to ask you few questions that might be general. Is it correct that all citizens of Macedonia of full age, after they served the conscription military service, are deployed within the reserve forces of the army of the Republic of Macedonia or the police of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
