utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The records of persons that are deployed within the reserve forces of the police as you have already mentioned, are maintained in the unit for defence preparations of either police stations and Ministry of Interior or in the sector for internal affairs of that region or of the city of Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the records for the reserve forces of the army of the Republic of Macedonia are maintained in the units of defence in certain municipalities in the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although this is not your own task but considering that you issued weapons also to the reserve forces, I would like to ask you whether it is correct that if some person wanted to change their post within the reserve forces that change could be introduced only by the unit for defence of the Ministry of Defence within a given municipality, upon a request of, let's say, the competent body of police that was dealing with defence preparations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to wrap up the general questions, is it correct that if the police would need a greater number of the members of the reserve forces or if the -- there would be a greater number of volunteers coming to the police, then the person in charge of defence preparations would need to submit a request to the Ministry of Defence to the unit within the municipality to deploy a certain number of officers to the police and that they are transferred from the list of the reserve army forces to the reserve police forces. Was that, in brief, the procedure that was necessary to be respected?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I suppose yes, although it is outside of my scope of competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that, in fact, the reserve forces of the police would be summoned also during peacetime in order for certain exercises to take place?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, only those persons would be called from the list of the reserve forces of the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the security situation when it was worsened, when the public order and peace is endangered or during wartime the members of the reserve forces would be called upon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they could have been called individually, or there could have been a general notice so that people would come to the positions where they have been allocated to, in the reserve forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering to the questions of my learned colleagues, you said that from around June in your police station a certain number of volunteers started to come who were willing to accept weapons or to be admitted into the reserve forces of the police. Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, I would like to ask you the following. Is it correct that in order for these volunteers who were not previously on the list of the reserve forces of the police, for them to be accepted in the reserve forces, it wasn't enough for them to be issued just weapons and uniforms, but they had to go through training to conduct the redistribution of their position or post in the reserve forces of the army to be entered in the reserve list of the police, to be allocated to certain tasks, and to receive payment for their engagement in the police, the so-called salary of the reserve forces, and, as you said a little bit later, for them to receive the ID of the reserve forces. Are these all the conditions that had to be met in order for a volunteer to become a member of the reserve forces of the police?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were saying the word "volunteers," if I understood it well, you were trying to say that these people, according to what you knew at that moment, at that moment they were not part of the reserve forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Not in the police, yes, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in order for them to become reservists in the police, they had to go through all of this training, to be deployed in the reserve forces of the police, they had to be on the list of the reserve forces of the police and they were supposed to receive salaries at the police; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were issuing weapons to these volunteers who arrived, you said that you did not issue IDs for two reasons: The first one because this was not your duty at all to issue special documents for identification; and, number two, because at that time such documents have not been prescribed yet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask for the witness to be shown Exhibit P85, please. This is ER 004 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters did not catch the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English is ER042. So Exhibit P85, Macedonian version page ER042-4706 and the English ER042-4706-ET.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, can you see in front of you this rule book?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which contains the form and the procedure for the issuance of a special document for the identification of the members of the reserve forces of the MOI. I will kindly ask for the document to be lifted upwards so that we can see the bottom of the page of this document. As you can see, this document is comprised on -- in July 2001 in Skopje. If we turn to the first page -- in fact, if we look at the second page, ER042-7408 and the English ER4704-ET [as interpreted]. One more page, if you can turn it, please. And the same page in English. ER042-4709-ET. While we turn to the next page in English, at the bottom of this Macedonian text, following Article 7, you can see the number of the document and you can see that it was issued on the 1st of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Stojanovski, is: Is it correct that until this date, if you can recall it, the volunteers who were coming, the overall procedure that we mentioned, had to be followed, but throughout this procedure they still could not get this document for identification because at that time it did not exist yet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that following this period, all the individuals who have been accepted in the reserve forces previously as well as the individuals who have been accepted following this document and its adoption, they had to be -- they had to accept this type of identification from the security preparation as a proof of their status in the reserve force of the police?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: According to the rule book, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as far as you know, this was followed in practice as well; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th and 26th of July when you issued the weapons to these individuals who came to the police station, as you mentioned earlier, in order for them to become part of the reserve force of the police, they had to fulfil some other conditions. However, is it correct that you were not the person who had to instruct them about all they have to do but this was the police station commander? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you individually did not and you were not obliged to check whether these people attended training, whether their position in the police reserve forces has been regulated or whether they have been included in the list of the reserve forces of the police. You have never, until the present date, checked this out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know at all whether these individuals at any time, all of them or some of them, whether they have been included in and registered in the reserve police forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, Mr. Stojanovski, that the act of issuing weapons and uniforms at your police station did not mean that the people received the status of reserve police officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was exactly identical for all other police stations and not just for yours. So also for the police station in Cair or Gazi Baba or any other police station, the actual receipt of the weapon was not a proof that a individual became a member of the reserve police forces of the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Responding to the question of my learned colleague, you said that Goran Stojkov in the fall sometime in 2001, he asked you to maintain the registry, the list of the Lions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, when they were established with a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I will ask to you look at the Exhibit 1D153. This is page N000-5388, the Macedonian; and the English version would be N000-5388-ET. Before you, you have the list of 182 individuals who have been hired in the Fast Response Unit Lions on the basis of the agreement provided by the Ministry of Finance number 19?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not catch the rest of the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of November, 2001. Can you please tell me, Mr. Stojanovski - and this is the 12th of November, 2001, thank you - is this the first list of the individuals who were members of the Fast Response Battalion, Lions, that you maintained later on and you updated the list with additional individuals who have been accepted at the Rapid Deployment Battalion later on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This was a list that was prepared by the sector for legal issues, according to the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what you said that sometime in the fall, November or December, you started maintaining the Lions lists as well. Then this review of the 182 persons would be a proof that only in November 2001 you started for the first time to maintain the records of the Lions, because this is the time when they were established. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, to a question of my learned colleague, you said that the members of the Rapid Deployment Battalion, Lions, received their weapon later on in Idrizovo. Is it correct, Mr. Stojanovski, that in your warehouses at PSOLO you had only a limited number or quantities of weapons which, after being handed out to the regular police forces and the volunteers who were coming to apply in smaller groups, you did not have any further weapons to be given out to other units? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To a question of my learned colleague related to the people who arrived on the 25th of July, the question whether you ever issued any weapons earlier to some organisations, you replied that they arrived as volunteers. To the subsequent question, if you ever issued any weapons to a group of people from a security organisation or any other organisation, earlier you said that this was the first time. My question, Mr. Stojanovski, is: Did you, at that time, issue the weapons to every single person individually as volunteers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, if I was ordered so. I would do that only upon orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you did not issue weapons at that time to any kind of organisation; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I issued the weapons to every single person individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You only knew from what you were told that they come from this security agency or organisation Kometa, but according to the rule, you issued the weapons to every single person individually as a individual volunteer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that there were groups of volunteers before coming to you and you issued weapons to them, would my conclusion, the one that I will say to you in a moment, be correct; namely, is it correct that due to the deteriorated security situation in the Republic of Macedonia, there was a huge dissatisfaction of the citizens. There were frequent protests and demonstrations that put also the government buildings that were under the competences of your police stations at risk. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct also that your police station needed additional forces so that you can perform your duties fully in such complex circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, since the active police officers were deployed in the field, in the fight against terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you, as a person who worked only on issuance and recording the issued weapons, were aware that that one part of the volunteers that used to come earlier would be subjected to the procedure and would become member of the reserve forces and would be then involved in carrying out some of the duties of your police station?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to say that the difference between those groups that came previously, as you stated in your statement earlier, in groups of five or ten people, and this group that came, for you the only difference was the number of them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't find anything strange in the situation that people came to enlist within the reserve forces, and they were needed to be issued with weapons and uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, as you stated, you never checked or you never knew and this is also not within your scope of competences to know whether these persons became reserve forces of the police at any time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Antonio Apostolski and I appear on behalf of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Together with me there is my colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic, who is also Defence counsel for Mr. Tarculovski. Before I start asking you questions, I would like to draw your attention as my colleague Edina Residovic had, that you speak my language, the Macedonian, I also understand the language that you will use in answering my questions, but I would like to ask you to wait for it to be interpreted into the other languages so that the interpreters are better able to interpret what we are saying. Witness, you work in the police station for external physical security of facilities as an administrator?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As my colleague stated, it is known as PSOLO?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the police station where you work, PSOLO, is at the foothill of the Vodno mountain?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is in the southern part of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the residence of the president of the Republic of Macedonia is in the immediate vicinity of the PSOLO station?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the president of the Republic of Macedonia, the late Boris Trajkovski, together with his family, in 2001, used to live in the residence that is located in the immediate vicinity of the PSOLO police station?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the security of the president, his personal security, the security for his family, often came to the police station where you worked and actively cooperated with them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is how you know Mr. Johan Tarculovski, as a body-guard for the president Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Johan Tarculovski came often to your station, PSOLO, where you were working?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you saw Mr. Johan Tarculovski there several times.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could it have happened that Johan Tarculovski was at the station at other times when weapons were issued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you have seen him on the 25th of July, Mr. Johan Tarculovski, in the yard of the station near the walnut tree?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that that place is different from the place where the group that was being issued with weapons was standing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: He was standing there alone. There was no one else next to him, and with regards to the group, some were inside, some were standing outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you did not see Mr. Johan Tarculovski talking to anyone of the group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P00379, marked for identification; otherwise 65 ter 285.11. We are waiting for the English version to appear on the screen. Could --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the Official Note on the screen, the one that my learned friend from the Prosecutor's office showed you before?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that there are several inaccuracies in this Official Note?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I stated this before, "led by" does not correspond to the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The first inaccuracy is that the person submitting this Official Note is Staff Sergeant Miodrag Stojanovski, police officer administrator?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Further on, it is incorrect that the volunteers led by Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is another inaccuracy and also you said that they -- that the list was submitted to the commander Georgi Mitrev. They presented a list?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this fact is also inaccurate in this Official Note. Also, you do not know whether your commander was in consultations with the superiors from the security sector before ordering you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I could not know, because I do not enter his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you can agree with me that there at least four facts in this Official Note that are inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I would like to ask you now, you answered a question by my learned colleague Edina Residovic that in the warehouse where the weapons were kept there were also pistols made by Zastava. Do you remember that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are these pistols made in Yugoslavia made in the city of Kragujevac, in Serbia, to be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the factory Zastava in Kragujevac, cars are made as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the cars of the make Zastava were produced before 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the cars Zastava are still produced until this very day in Kragujevac?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I do have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, were you asked by my learned colleague Ms. Residovic about whether you had ever received orders yourself from the Minister of the Interior. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you said that, no, you never received orders yourself; do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: It is correct. I received orders only from my superior officer. This is what the hierarchy structure is like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And isn't the hierarchical structure also that the minister would issue orders. They would not go to you but they would go to your superiors; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: That -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: You were also asked about what would happen if there was a breach of discipline by a member of the Ministry of the Interior. And this is at page 41. You were asked whether it was the case that only the immediate superior could investigate disciplinary proceedings. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if I understand correctly you agreed with my learned colleague that it would be only the immediate superior who would instigate disciplinary proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, what would happen if a member of the Ministry of the Interior committed some act against the rules of the ministry and this was discovered by someone perhaps above his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I am an ordinary police officer. I'm not a superior officer to make that assessment, what would happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, as far as you are aware, if the Minister of Interior himself became aware of a breach of the rules of discipline of the ministry would be able to instigate disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I could not answer this. This is outside of my scope of competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, then, if we can revisit what you said so my learned colleague, would it then be fair to say that your response to her question was also outside your scope of knowledge? You don't really know what the situation is, as far as disciplinary proceedings goes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I said that I was aware of the disciplinary procedures. The commander is the one instigating the disciplinary procedure for his subordinate officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And so is it your testimony that someone above a person's immediate superior does not have the authority to instigate disciplinary proceedings, or you simply don't know?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: They could possibly order the one below them, so they then instigate a disciplinary procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, you were also asked some questions by my learned colleague about the procedure for issuing weapons and whether volunteers who were issued with weapons were considered to be members of the reservists. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, these people who came to PSOLO and who were issued with weapons, these volunteers, the uniforms that they were issued with, would they be any different to what the regular reservists were wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would the automatic weapons that they carried, would be they different to what the regular reservists were using?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, for example, to a general member of the public would there be any way for them to tell the difference between the volunteers and regular reservists?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And what would that be?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: There is no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And prior to the point where identification cards were issued, which I believe the order showed to be in August 2001, did volunteers ever join up with units of the reserve or active police?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: The volunteers were sent to Idrizovo, because accommodation and provision were provided there so that they would undergo the police train and they would be redeployed from the reserve forces of the army or whether they were into the reserve forces of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And once they were redeployed would they be expected to follow the orders and instructions of the commanders of the units they were deployed to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And when you issued weapons and other equipment, uniforms and such to volunteers, was this done with the intention that these people would be deployed to reserve or regular units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: This is not within my competences. The superior officer who ordered me to issue them with weapons knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, from your knowledge of how the Ministry of the Interior works or how the police force works, would you expect that your superiors would give orders for civilians to be able to roam the streets of Macedonia in uniform -- in police uniform and with police weapons without them actually being part of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And by my learned colleague Mr. Apostolski were asked some question about the presence of Mr. Tarculovski at the police station, at PSOLO, on 25th of July. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it was your testimony at that point that he was standing alone by a walnut tree and was not with anyone else; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, do you recall earlier on when I was asking you questions being shown -- refreshing your memory with part of your statement in which it said that Mr. Tarculovski had led the group, had come with the group of Kometa employees to the police station. Do you recall where it said that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So are you saying that that was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not see them arriving, so I cannot really say whether he came with them or not. I was in my office, and only when I got out I could see the people and himself. I did not see them earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Was he mingling with these other people?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, again, I need to ask you this, and I want you to answer this question. The part of your statement that you were shown which said that Mr. Tarculovski and the Kometa people arrived together, are you saying that that is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: If I saw them coming, then I could have said that they arrived together, but I did not see them arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, again, please answer this with a yes or no. Is that part of your statement that was shown incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: No, it is not incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And are you saying that's as a result of a misunderstanding by the investigator who interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: I told you that Mr. Thomas or -- was making a lot of corrections and at the end it was rather late and I was tired and all, and the statement was not read to me again. I just signed the statement and we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you also recall being shown a document which is marked for identification as P00379, the information on the activities undertaken by the investigate committee where it stated that you provided the information to them that Johan Tarculovski led the group of Kometa employees. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that they also were mistaken on this one particular point?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you were shown the Official Note, which is also marked for identification as part of the -- the exhibit marked for identification as P00379, which states it was submitted by you but you have testified was not. And, again, that contained the information that Johan Tarculovski led the group of Kometa employees. Do you remember seeing that document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that whoever did prepare this particular note, was also mistaken on that specific point?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: What is missing is my written statement. It is obvious that the committee did not provide it to you, which is the most relevant one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: But, again, my question is a little more specific than that. Are you saying that at that particular point whoever prepared that note was mistaken also?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STOJANOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much Mr. Dobbyn. Mr. Stojanovski, thank you very much for the help that you have given to this Court. This brings your evidence to an end, and you may now withdraw. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours I would like to propose for the Exhibit 1D146 MFI that marked for identification on the 3rd of September, 2007, this is page of the transcript 4.519, which has been shown to the witness, Eichner, to be accepted as evidence. On this page the proposal was for this document to be just marked for identification until the corrected interpretation is not received from the CLSS. Now this updated translation is accepted to 1D00- --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so we would like ask for the translation to be replaced. I will repeat the number of the corrected, 1D00-8184, and we kindly ask, first of all, for the previous translation to be replaced and, number two, for this document to be accepted into evidence. Otherwise this was document which was earlier on the 65 ter list of the Prosecution under number 69. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under the same number, that would be 1D146, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon. The Prosecution, I believe, expected the present witness to take a little bit longer. However Mr. Bezruchenko could resume his testimony. I believe we were checking with the Defence to see whether or not they were in a position though to start that today or tomorrow. I believe Ms. Guduric was sending an email as the -- Mr. Stojanovski was testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I turn now to Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague Guenael Mettraux who is cross-examining the witness, the expert witness, Mr. Bezruchenko, is not present in The Hague and he won't be present until Sunday, and these were the reasons why the Defence counsel of Mr. Boskoski asked for the cross-examination of this witness to be continued on Monday. Therefore, we would like to ask for the Trial Chamber to approve this delay for the cross-examination until Monday, because the purpose, and bearing in mind the fact that the cross-examination is being conducted by Mr. Mettraux, it would not be possible for us to continue with the cross-examination today and tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: So I understand that, Mr. Apostolski, would not be ready to start your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we sent a e-mail to Ms. Guduric and we informed them that we are not capable of starting interviewing this -- questioning this witness tomorrow and bearing in mind the load, the volume of the questions to be asked, after all, I would propose the Trial Chamber to postpone his -- his testimony until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, then, the Trial Chamber can't do anything else than adjourn for the rest of the week, and we will resume on a Monday morning at 9.00. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.32 p.m.,
